name: Phantom of the Opera
beta:
On the first pitch, climb the face and faint crack up and left, then traverse left across Kreuser's Chimney into a horizontal crack. Follow it left to a vertical fingercrack and climb that to a ledge belay.

The second pitch goes up the face with two bolts to a thin crack leaning rightward, crosses it, and keeps on up the face above.
overview: The R is mostly bluff: the runout part is modest, around 5.7, and avoidable. The first pitch starts on a face and crack, crosses Kreuser's Chimney into a horizontal crack, then a thin finger crack to the belay. The second goes up the face with a pair of bolts to a thin crack.

name: Piggys Conch Shell
beta: On the northeast flank, get over the rubble at the base, then follow the shallow trough worn smooth by water, clipping two bolts, to a small crack. Keeping to the trough's left side gives the 5.8 climbing.
overview: A slick, water-worn groove with two bolts leads to a small crack. Edging up its left side keeps the climb at 5.8, whereas sticking to the slick groove itself is far harder. A sloping ledge and a big block carrying bolt number three complete the route.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: On the hill's northeast flank, once past the rubble at the bottom

name: Good Vibrations
beta: Start twenty feet right of Rastaman Vibration and follow the broken crack and the face, clipping the one bolt, to the top of the slab.
overview: A bold line up a broken crack and face to the top of a slab, with a single bolt. Its first ascensionist soloed it on a rope, expecting a second bolt higher up that turned out not to exist.

current.area_walk_in: From the trailhead, follow the main park trail and look for the spur marked for climbing access, which leads to the peak from the east. Another way is to take the wide cart path from the visitor center to the first climbers' trail sign, then head up and left toward the peak.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.detailed_rack: A bolted anchor, three good bolts, and .2/small nuts.
current.location: About 6 m right of Rastaman Vibration

name: Happy Robots
beta: West of the Sun Deck Boulder, climb the eighty-foot buttress facing south, beginning at its lower left and angling up and rightward. There is one bolt low on the route.
overview: An 80 ft south-facing buttress, climbed from its lower left corner, trending upward to the right.

current.area_walk_in: From the trailhead, follow the main park trail and look for the spur marked for climbing access, which leads to the peak from the east. Another way is to take the wide cart path from the visitor center to the first climbers' trail sign, then head up and left toward the peak.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Out On A Limb
beta: Start at the southeast-facing pillar and climb the arete that leans rightward, passing one bolt, to a horizontal crack. Move left to a ledge and finish up an easy hand crack.
overview: Climb an arete that leans right past a bolt to a horizontal crack, move left to a ledge, and finish by an easy hand crack.

current.area_walk_in: From the trailhead, follow the main park trail and look for the spur marked for climbing access, which leads to the peak from the east. Another way is to take the wide cart path from the visitor center to the first climbers' trail sign, then head up and left toward the peak.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: roughly 200 ft downhill of South Crack, at a pillar facing southeast

name: Rastaman Vibration
beta: Start at the left side of the white slab and climb the face, clipping three bolts, to the top.

current.area_walk_in: From the trailhead, follow the main park trail and look for the spur marked for climbing access, which leads to the peak from the east. Another way is to take the wide cart path from the visitor center to the first climbers' trail sign, then head up and left toward the peak.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: left side of a white slab, roughly 100 feet west and below Brown Out

name: Thundering Hearts
beta: Begin as Shalayly Direct does and follow that route to its third bolt, then descend a little and cross rightward past a bolt, making this a long girdle-style line.
overview: Intended as a marvellous girdle traverse. Climb Shalayly Direct to its third bolt (5.11a), then downclimb a little and traverse rightward.

current.area_walk_in: From the trailhead, follow the main park trail and look for the spur marked for climbing access, which leads to the peak from the east. Another way is to take the wide cart path from the visitor center to the first climbers' trail sign, then head up and left toward the peak.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: shares its start with Shalayly Direct

name: Power Hungry
beta: Pitch one is a steep face, and a #1 Friend can ease the nerves at the eighth bolt. Once the bolts run out, pitch two is thinly protected though only 5.6, and most parties just run it out.
overview: A long, steep face climb; the second pitch runs out on easy 5.6 terrain once the bolts stop, and the best finish moves around onto the upper pitch of Metro.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.detailed_rack: Draws; a #1 Friend helps near the eighth bolt on the opening pitch
current.location: Right-hand bolts, reached via a ramp at the start, on Punch and Judy Towers' right portion.

name: Not! Pregnant Lizard
beta: Midway up the south face, pass two replaced bolts to a sloping shelf. From there, aid past more bolts, under the overhang and then to the summit.
overview: On the south face's midsection, pass two replaced bolts to a sloping shelf, then aid along bolts into the roof and finish at the top.

current.area_walk_in: Follow the standard Echo Canyon hiking trail up to the Headwall, then climb one of the Headwall routes (a short fourth-class scramble, with bolts) to reach the plateau where the tower stands.

name: Question of Balance
beta: Stay mostly on the right side of the buttress dividing the south and east faces, moving leftward away from the corner system solely to reach the belay. From the belay, swing back round onto the east face and climb on until you spot the bolt.
overview: Follows a corner system right of the south/east buttress, steps left to belay, then returns onto the east face past a bolt.

current.area_walk_in: Pass on the west side behind Mean Mistreater Wall, then descend through the gap separating Faded Rock from Obscure Rock.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: Just to the right side of the buttress dividing the south and east faces

name: Quickdraw McGraw
beta: Begin beside the big pine, on its right, and head diagonally rightward toward the conspicuous weak spot in the wall, then look for the bolts. A beeline to those bolts often turns out to be the wrong choice. Small wired nuts cover the opening moves.
overview: Angles rightward and up to the obvious weak point in the face, then you must find the bolts; heading straight for each is often not the best line. Wired nuts cover the early moves.

current.area_walk_in: A gully descends to the foot of the cliff; the short walk is worth it.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: beside the large pine, on its right

name: Red Tail Diner
beta: Reach the tree from its right side, then climb the awkward hand crack right behind it, ending on a small platform. The second pitch traverses left from the ledge to a thin crack that leads to the summit, with micro-nuts protecting the crux friction moves.
overview: Named for hawks seen in the area. The first pitch is an awkward hand crack right behind the tree; the second pitch is a classic that moves left on a ledge, then follows a slender crack to the summit, with micro-nuts on the hard moves.

current.detailed_rack: Pitch 1 takes #.5 up to 3 Bd; pitch 2 takes micro nuts and micro cams up to #1 Bd.
current.location: From the tree reached by scrambling up from its right side

name: Renaissance Direct
beta: On the first pitch climb the face, clipping two bolts, to a ledge, continue up the dihedral that faces right, over a little roof to another ledge, then move left to the belay. The second pitch climbs the face above, with four bolts, to the top.
overview: Alternating between face and crack, this is among the most pleasing lines on the wall. Two bolts protect the opening face to a ledge, a dihedral with its corner facing right leads over a small roof, and four more bolts cover the face above.

name: Reunion
beta: Start at the foot of the buttress with three cracks that arch rightward, facing east, and climb the face immediately to the left of the leftmost crack. Take the easiest path; heading straight for the bolt makes it harder than the grade.
overview: The route follows the face left from the leftmost crack. Find the easiest path; heading directly for the bolt feels nearer to 5.9. Bolts were stripped by someone unknown, so it is now toprope only.

current.descent: short rappel from the eyebolt on top
current.location: Below a buttress whose east face has three bold cracks curving rightward

name: Ridgeback
beta: Follow the left-hand arete of the buttress straight up its seven bolts.
overview: An excellent first lead with big views, up the left arete of the buttress beside the main cliff to the east.

current.area_walk_in: From the foot of the main cliff go down the gully, then swing leftward around the corner beneath the neighbouring buttress.
current.descent: rap 15 m (50 ft) west from the summit bolts
current.location: Left-hand arete of the next buttress downhill; the main cliff lies to its west

name: Rossetti Rose
beta: A short dihedral gets you started, then step right past a bolt to the base of the thin crack. Follow it past three fixed pins to a big ledge, where the face above leads to the top of the West Summit.
overview: A thin-crack test piece that began life as an aid line before being freed, high on the West Summit of the peak. The sustained difficulty is the thin crack above a ledge system, where several fixed pitons are already in place.

current.area_walk_in: From the trailhead, follow the main park trail and look for the spur marked for climbing access, which leads to the peak from the east. Another way is to take the wide cart path from the visitor center to the first climbers' trail sign, then head up and left toward the peak.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: About 15 m up and right of Parallax View

name: Rurpture
beta: A brief, bolt-protected face section holds the crux and leads to a crack arching rightward. Follow that crack until you can move straight up the face over a horizontal crack to the top.
overview: Named for the bolt, drilled with the driller's weight on a small RURP piton in a seam. Initially graded 5.8, it was raised after a key foothold snapped. A brief bolt-protected face gains a crack curving right, then the face goes direct past a horizontal break.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: Just right of Varicose

name: Sacred Datura Direct
beta: Climb a small dihedral until you can step right onto the face, then clip a bolt and slant rightward into a second vertical crack. Follow it to an alcove, take the crack and face above to a horizontal break with a bolt, and finish on small discontinuous cracks.
overview: Continuous climbing on good rock, mixing crack and face. Two bolts supplement the gear.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: About 20 feet right of Ubangy Lips, up a small dihedral

name: Dado
beta: Follow the corner, which stays overhanging, clipping three bolts and a fixed pin on the way to the top. The name refers to the shallow dihedral formed by the upper corner.
overview: Follows a corner that overhangs more and more, passing bolts and a fixed pin. The shallow dihedral high up gives the route its name.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: adjacent to Thrash Compactor, at the formation's southwest corner

name: Famous Last Moves
beta: Start in a finger seam and follow it up. The finish leaves a scoop and goes onto the face, passing one bolt.
overview: A short finger-seam line on the right side of the formation, with the interest saved for the final moves.

current.descent: rappel off the north side from a sling on a boulder
current.location: Right-hand route on the small formation stacked atop the Mish Mash buttress

name: Mish Mash
beta: Begin with a finger-width crack starting off a boulder and follow it up a steep runnel, clipping two or three bolts. Stay in the seam, where aluminum bashies help, as far as bolt three, then step right and finish by clipping the final bolt.
overview: A pleasant route up a light-colored runnel, steep in its middle section and finished at a tree belay. Protected by a mix of bolts and small to medium gear.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: Off a boulder at the base, in the pale runnel just left of the alcove with the hanging beehive

name: The Panty Route
beta: Climb the gentle slab to a flake with a single bolt, then angle up and rightward, clipping the second bolt, to the top.
overview: Low-angle face climbing leads past a bolt to a flake, then the line angles rightward past a second bolt to the top.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: lower than the Mish Mash start, on a little slab formation

name: Seam-In
beta: Climb the face with one bolt to a thin crack, which holds the crux. Follow the crack leftward, clipping two fixed pitons, until you can join Dog Fight Giggle, then take its thin crack to the top.
overview: Starts up the face with a bolt, enters a thin crack that holds the crux, and slants left by two fixed pins to merge with the neighbouring line for the finish.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: Thirty ft along on the right from Dog Fight Giggle

name: Sideshow
beta: Climb the arete alongside Kate's Fault, clipping two bolts on the way up. Gear is needed to build the belay.
overview: A two-bolt arete beside the main wall; bring gear for the belay.

current.descent: walk off either end of the wall

name: Silhouette
beta: Ascend roughly 45 feet of South Crack's upper pitch, then step left onto the arete and climb its face, clipping three bolts, to a horizontal crack. Reach right to clip the last bolt and go straight up from there; moving right after that clip makes it easier.
overview: Branch left from South Crack onto an arete with three bolts, up to a horizontal crack. Work toward its right-hand end to clip the last bolt, then go directly up. It is easier if you drift right after that last clip, but the line goes straight.

current.area_walk_in: From the trailhead, follow the main park trail and look for the spur marked for climbing access, which leads to the peak from the east. Another way is to take the wide cart path from the visitor center to the first climbers' trail sign, then head up and left toward the peak.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: after roughly 45 feet of South Crack pitch two, move left onto the arete

name: Smooth Sailing
beta: Start at an open book and climb the dihedral to a stance with a bolt. From there continue to a horizontal break and follow it rightward to a clear belay.
overview: A dihedral leads to a stance with a bolt, then a horizontal crack is followed rightward to an obvious belay.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: Roughly 20 ft over from Thin Air, at an open book

name: Snakes are Poodles Too
beta: Take the thin crack system on the east face's right side up to a ledge, then keep going on the crack onto the face and past a bolt to a second ledge. Cross the face over a boulder, passing one more bolt, to the top.
overview: A thin crack to a ledge, more crack into face past a bolt, then over a boulder past a second bolt.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: Right side of the east face

name: Femme Fatale
beta: Pitch one goes up a face to a crack and a pin under a bulge, with the belay in the alcove above it. Pitch two steps right of the vegetated crack onto the face and heads up to a bolt, with another runout beyond.
overview: Two-pitch line: face moves lead into a crack and a fixed pin below a bulge, with a stance in an alcove over it. The second pitch moves off a grassy crack onto runout face climbing past a lone bolt.

current.area_walk_in: Aim for the thumb-shaped tower, then take a trail leftward that runs above the neighbouring gully, to arrive on top of this fin; a class 4 scramble down its left side leads to the cliff base. For climbs on the north side of the fin, descend the gully separating the two fins.

name: Static Cling
beta:
Pitch one follows a small crack, then traverses left to a bolt and goes past a catclaw tree to a crack and belay. Pitch two climbs the crack until it ends, face-climbs rightward and upward to a ramp and crack, follows the ramp to a horn, then steps left and finishes up a fingercrack.

The final pitch ascends a crack that arches rightward to the top.
overview: Varied free-climbing, with a small crack to a leftward traverse to a bolt, a catclaw tree, then a crack and ramp to a horn, a fingercrack, and a final arching crack.

current.location: Approximately 15 ft over from Triple J Direct

name: Stems and Seeds
beta: Climb a dihedral and crack up to a belay on two bolts. Then step left and take an offwidth to a ramp leading to the summit, or take the steep, shallow crack on its left.
overview: A dihedral and crack lead to a two-bolt stance; the second pitch steps left into an offwidth and a ramp to the summit.

current.detailed_rack: A pair of bolts on the big ledge up top serve as top anchor; belay from a pair of bolts at the stance beneath the large roof. Gear: standard, to 4 inches. Hardware renewed 2025.

name: Coloring Book
beta: Climb the dihedral made by the flake's right side to a ledge, then carefully work up the fractured spike under the roof. Follow the roof crack leftward; at its end either bail leftward into the gully, or move right onto the face and clip two bolts.
overview: A south-facing roof-and-dihedral line with a flake start and a crack that cuts out through the roof. The finish offers a choice between a grungy gully exit and a bolted face exit.

current.area_walk_in: Loose soil and rock below these crags makes walking up damaging and sometimes dangerous, so anchors are placed on top. Gear up above, descend by rope to the base, then climb back up to your packs.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Tears of a Clown
beta: Start on a pillar left of Edge, climb to a bolt, then shift left and climb to a ledge belay. The headwall above is tackled once you have clipped a bolt; the run-out section comes on the moves below the first bolt.
overview: Up past a bolt, left to a belay ledge, then a headwall protected by another bolt; mixed gear.

current.area_walk_in: Walk past the restrooms and follow the clear path along the ridge, away from the road, to the big pinnacle called Nancy's Thumb. Descend the steep gully beneath it; the routes line the wall to your right.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: From the pillar immediately left of The Edge of Da-light

name: The Bickerson's Dirty Habits
beta: Parallel cracks lead to a flake crack and then a horizontal one. Move up to a bolt on the face, clip a second, and continue to the top, exiting rightward.
overview: Thin, steep and demanding to lead: parallel cracks join a flake crack, then a horizontal crack, with a step up to a bolt on the face and a second bolt above before an exit to the right.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: Close to five ft along from the Low Road line

name: The Chute
beta: Climb the face, clipping two bolts, to a horizontal crack, then continue on the face past another bolt to ledges.
overview: Face climbing with two bolts reaches a horizontal crack, then a third bolt takes you to ledges.

current.area_walk_in: Head east on the Marcus Landslide trail for roughly a third of a mile, then turn right at the Sven Slab sign. Loop around a big boulder and over a low rise, then pick up the climbers' path on the right toward the Nit Nat flake. Many informal tracks dead-end in brush; if you are squeezing through thick scrub, turn back.
current.descent: scramble down the gully to the left

name: Crazy Man Driver
beta: Take the detached flake, then make a delicate step left onto the face and go on to the upper face, passing a pair of fixed pins and one bolt. Two more bolts lead to the top.
overview: Starts up a vertical stretch of detached flake, then makes a risky step left onto the face, clips a bolt and two pins already in place, and two more bolts lead to the top. Whether it earns its R is debated.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Geronimo’s Cadillac
beta: Follow a crack of finger to hand size until it ends, then reach a bolt and head up the face to a broken section. Another bolt protects the face above and the step across the chasm; the top section is easy ground but unprotected.
overview: A finger-to-hand crack on the central buttress fades into bolted face, then crosses a gap and runs out on easy ground to the top.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: Central buttress, immediately right of the roof line

name: Wotme Two Step
beta: Climb the face and detached flake until a step right gets you into a scoop. Then go up the face, drifting slightly rightward, clipping two bolts to the top.
overview: Climbs face and flake, steps into a scoop to the right, then continues up the face with two bolts. A large exfoliated flake sits nearby.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: Immediately beyond Crazy Man Driver, up a detached flake bordering the tan rock

name: Blind Faith
beta: Pitch one follows an obvious crack of hand and finger size until it ends, then moves left across the face past a bolt to the arete, merging with Indecent Exposure by its third clip. Pitch two is that route's upper part, to the summit.
overview: Follow the obvious crack, taking hands and fingers, until it ends; then angle left on the face past a bolt to the arete and merge with Indecent Exposure on reaching that route's third bolt. Pitch two is the top of that route.

current.area_walk_in: No established climber trails lead in, though a fairly good game trail traces the high side of the gully to the foot of the rock.
current.location: 25 ft over from Indecent Exposure, in the middle of the face making up the big dihedral's left-hand wall

name: Crater Maker
beta: Open with a crack and some face to a bolt, then angle up and rightward across the face, clipping three more, to the arete. Follow the arete past a horizontal crack and one more bolt; the angle eases near the top. Extra bolts were added to remove the original X rating.
overview: Crack and face lead to a bolt, then three more bolts angle rightward and upward onto an arete, which is followed past a horizontal crack and one more bolt to easier ground at the top.

current.area_walk_in: No established climber trails lead in, though a fairly good game trail traces the high side of the gully to the foot of the rock.
current.descent: walk off northwest from the top
current.location: centre of the face that forms the right wall of the big dihedral

name: Deviant Behavior
beta: Climb the face past the first bolt, where the crux sits, to gain a horizontal crack and the arete. Stay on the arete, clipping two more bolts, until you merge with Crater Maker.
overview: A route that follows the obvious arete formed by the dihedral's right wall. The crux is the face move to the first bolt, and the route merges higher with Crater Maker.

current.area_walk_in: No established climber trails lead in, though a fairly good game trail traces the high side of the gully to the foot of the rock.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: right side of the large dihedral at the base of the wall
